Internal steps of reverse mapping walk and per-mapping clean callbacks and veto predicate.
Lock ordering guarantees among folio lock, mapping locks, hugetlb lock, failure mutex and frame-space lock.
Layouts of folio, page, area, address space, device pagemap, kill entry and frame-space structures.
Semantics of unmap flags, failure flags, poison message codes and result codes.
Driver-specific device failure handlers and direct-access entry lock mechanics.
Debugfs operation tables for corrupt and unpoison controls and filter predicate details.

Page-table and scheduler identifier initialization hidden behind architecture macros.

findings.text: Public helpers for reverse mapping and poisoning: address lookup from folio plus page plus area, folio cleaning walk, poisoned folio unmapping, and mapping range unmapping are globally visible routines callable from other memory management parts.
Hardware poison control surface: software unpoison by frame number, registration and removal of poison filter callback, and device pagemap lookup plus range validity test are globally visible.
Initial address space object and its early setup routine plus a placeholder area operations object are globally visible; setup records code start and end plus data end and break values.

Address lookup distinguishes anonymous and file backed areas: anonymous requires both sides to carry an anonymous structure with the same root, file backed requires an attached file whose mapping matches the folio mapping, otherwise a fault error is reported; offset derives from folio plus page position.

Cleaning requires the folio to be locked and to be currently mapped with a resolved mapping; unmapped or mapping-less folios return a zero cleaned count without walking; otherwise a reverse walk applies per-mapping cleaning and per-area veto and returns total cleaned.

Poison unmapping starts with ignore-locked plus synchronous plus poison flags; swap cache entries retain poison and lose the poison-unmap flag; clean writeback-capable folios that stay clean after a cleaning pass also lose the flag and are dropped quietly, while dirtied ones keep it; shared hugetlb takes the mapping write lock at a higher level and marks the walk as already locked, returning busy if that lock or any mapping remains.

Huge page acquisition for poisoning classifies the target as non-huge, already counted in use, freed, migratable acquired in use, or retry; poison tracking update can override the result with folio-level or page-level pre-poisoned; counted migratable folios have migratable cleared and report that clearing to the caller.

Raw poison tracking sets a folio poisoned marker and records the individual subpage; a second report for the same folio or same subpage is reported as pre-poisoned; if the unreliable marker is already set no new record is added; allocation failure sets unreliable and discards existing records.

Software unpoison only proceeds for an online poisoned page with no extra references, not slab nor page table nor reserved nor offline, not mapped and with no attached mapping, and only when no real hardware failure has occurred and the target is not the huge zero folio; hugetlb additionally requires a non-empty raw list to free.

Device pagemap validity scans configured ranges for containment and additionally requires the frame to be at or beyond the first usable frame, where only range zero is shifted by an alternative map offset; byte range unmapping converts to page units with rounding up and clamps an overflowing end to the addressable maximum.

Device pagemap failure rejects frames outside metadata, prefers a driver handler when present and falls back to a generic kill path only on unsupported, and forces action-required plus must-kill semantics because no replacement page can be swapped in; direct frame-space failures similarly force killing after collecting affected processes.

Architecture context initializer for the initial address space expands to nothing in this configuration, the internal header guard defines its marker, and a dummy area operations object exists as a shared placeholder; unpoison diagnostic logging emits only when a rate limiter allows.

Folio and page exclusion: cleaning asserts locked, huge-page splitting and process collection hold the folio lock across the operation, poison handling uses the folio lock around filter and mapping steps, and direct-access pages use a folio cookie lock instead of the page lock.

Mapping and global exclusion: shared hugetlb poison unmapping holds the mapping write lock externally, reverse collection holds the mapping read lock, frame-space iteration holds its mutex, unpoison holds the memory-failure mutex, free-huge dissolution disables per-cpu caches, and huge acquisition holds the hugetlb spin lock with interrupts disabled.

Read-copy-update and reference discipline: device pagemap lookup runs under read lock with a live reference attempt, process collection for frame spaces runs under read lock, filter registration and removal use assign plus null with synchronization, kill entries take a task reference, and conditional page references are released only when the counted flag is set.

Initial address space static initializer wires a maple tree to its own lock, points page tables at the swapper root, sets user count two and structural count one, initializes write-protect sequence, mmap lock, page-table and argument spin locks and module list, with optional per-area writer wait plus sequence and scheduler identifier lock, plus flexible array and architecture context placeholders.
Boot-time huge page descriptor holds an intrusive list node, a pointer to its state object, and a flags word.

Huge-page failure starts with acquisition, then branches to normal-page fallback, single retry, pre-poisoned kill-or-report, filtered unsupported, free-page dissolve handling, unmap-failed reporting, or page-state identification; free handling recovers only when dissolution plus buddy removal succeeds; an alternate configuration always takes the normal-page fallback.

Page-state identification scans a mask plus result table first with live flags then with saved flags merged with the live dirty bit, then invokes the matched action which leaves the page unlocked, and finally folds the action outcome plus message type into a reported result.

Generic device kill locks the folio, applies the poison filter, rejects private and coherent device types, marks poisoned, collects interested processes, unmaps the largest recorded mapping size aligned to the folio index, and then signals the collected tasks.

Test entry points create a poison directory with corrupt and unpoison controls plus enable, device identity, flag mask and value, and optional memory-group filters, and register a filter callback; removal clears enable, unregisters the callback, and deletes the directory; the unpoison control requires administrative privilege.
Early initialization entry records code, data and break boundaries into the initial address space; a tiny helper re-enables reclaim by dropping a disable count.

Races and failure modes include dirty state that may be set outside the page lock, unreliable raw poison history after allocation failure that blocks later free or dissolve, atomic allocation failures that skip killing or recording, reference-count versus mapping checks that can race with concurrent grabs, and address translation that can report fault for unmapped offsets.

Splitting and dissolution hazards include huge-page split that must hold the page lock and optionally drops a reference only on failure, free huge-page handling that races with allocation or demotion unless poisoned, and unmapping that must use the largest mapping size to avoid fragmenting fixed-size device mappings.
Reclaim mode bits use second and third bit positions for may-swap and proactive; swappiness ranges from zero to two hundred with anonymous-only defined as one past the maximum.
